clue.text: Snack sprightly bachelor brought in for maiden (6)

indicators.note: one letter is brought into the word in place of another

blocks.note: B = bachelor, as in degrees like BA
M = maiden, the cricket scorecard abbreviation; this M goes out

explanation.surface: Someone lively nips in to grab a bite on behalf of a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, recorded as M, so the young woman of the surface is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small bite taken between meals is a snack, and the verb matches the verb.

clue.text: Invalid turned firearm on a Conservative (8)

indicators.note: turned round, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An invalid pulls a gun on a Conservative politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' tempts you to read it as a sick person, the noun; it is the adjective, meaning without legal force.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for something of no force or worth, used of laws and agreements that do not hold.

clue.text: Erect barriers around security device in poor quarter (8)

indicators.note: the first piece sits inside the second

blocks.note: E = east, one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Put up barriers round a lock in a rundown part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor quarter' reads as a slum, but it splits into two pieces: an adjective and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb for sealing off a port or town, which is done by ringing it with ships, troops or barriers.

clue.text: Find execrable, old articles supporting Liberal (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports stands underneath, so L comes first

blocks.note: the indefinite article A and the definite article THE

explanation.surface: Someone decides old pieces backing the Liberals are dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, pieces that support another are written beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for hate intensely; execrable means detestable, so finding a thing so is detesting it.

clue.text: Posted wrong information initially about authoritarian (8)

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order
take the first letter only

explanation.surface: Someone put out misinformation about an autocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is fake news on social media; 'about' gives the letter C (circa, as in dates) and joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a despot rules with absolute power, which is what authoritarian describes.

clue.text: Almost stripped man of nobility (4)

indicators.note: its outer layer taken off, so first and last letters go

explanation.surface: A nobleman has had nearly everything taken off him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost stripped' looks like one idea, nearly naked; 'Almost' is the word to strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this British peer ranks between marquess and viscount.

clue.text: Blemish Spooner's artificial gardens (8)

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: mock = artificial; it takes the P from the next word
a park is public gardens; it takes the M

explanation.surface: A flaw in someone's fake gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: The two opening consonants trade places, which is all Spooner ever did.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the pitted scar left by smallpox or acne is a blemish on the skin.

clue.text: Model put on slip in panic (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is placed on top of the other

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
a slip is a small error

explanation.surface: A fashion model puts on a slip and panics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' and 'slip' paint a catwalk and a petticoat; the model is Ford's car and the slip a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name overwhelming fear.

clue.text: Partial apology struck revolutionary as show of respect (6)

indicators.note: only part of the words is used
turned right round, so read backwards

blocks.note: the last letter of apology and the first five of struck

explanation.surface: A half-hearted apology hit a revolutionary as a token of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a rebel receiving the apology; it tells you to read the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: bending the knees and bobbing down is a traditional gesture of deference.

clue.text: German graduate entertained by highly amusing international (6)

indicators.note: held inside, as a guest is entertained within a house

blocks.note: LOL = laugh out loud, texting slang

explanation.surface: A German graduate is entertained by something very funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertained' fits the hilarity in the surface, but it is a container instruction: the host holds the guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: worldwide reach spans nations, so the adjectives overlap.

clue.text: One who gets runs after treatment by professional (8)

indicators.note: 'after' in its sense of following in time, so R is written following CURE
'by' in its sense of alongside, so PRO stands next to the rest

blocks.note: a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: A patient gets the runs after treatment by a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' suggests an upset stomach after treatment; it is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent noun of procure, to obtain, so literally one who obtains.

clue.text: Italicus is in Paris defending Thailand's religious society (7)

definitions.note: the Society of Jesus is singular; its members, the Jesuits, are plural

indicators.note: 'in Paris' asks how the words would be said in the French capital, so translate into French
the outer word guards the inner letter

blocks.note: the setter Italicus says 'I am', in French je suis
T is Thailand's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: The setter is in Paris, protecting a Thai religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter names himself, so 'Italicus is' means 'I am', which a Parisian would say as je suis.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of the Society of Jesus, the Catholic order founded by Ignatius Loyola, standing for the order itself.

clue.text: Uneven track wends around East Herefordshire's borders? Pay attention! (4,4)

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters
the outer letters go round the inner ones
only the edge letters of the word

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of track wends
first and last letters of Herefordshire

explanation.surface: A bumpy track winds round the edge of eastern Herefordshire, so watch out!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uneven track' looks like a rough road; 'uneven' means odd-numbered letters, running across both words. Herefordshire is an English county on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase is an old-fashioned command to be careful and listen.

clue.text: Decorate rear of cab in some backward society (6)

indicators.note: B goes inside the reversed word
'backward' in its sense of facing the wrong way, so SOME is read from the end

explanation.surface: Adorning the back of a taxi in a society stuck in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward society' reads as one idea, a primitive culture; 'backward' belongs to 'some', and S for society simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific kind of decorating: raising a design in relief on metal, leather or paper.

clue.text: Expert claims referee's assistant essentially committed sin (7)

indicators.note: takes hold of, so the other letters go inside
at its essence, the middle letter

blocks.note: VAR = video assistant referee, used in football

explanation.surface: A pundit claims the video referee essentially committed a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: VAR is the video assistant referee who reviews football incidents.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: greed is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Ignorant schoolmarm is penniless (4)

indicators.note: loses its P, the abbreviation for penny

blocks.note: a schoolmarm is a prim, prudish type

explanation.surface: A strict old-fashioned teacher is uneducated and broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schoolmarm' suggests a teacher, but here it means a prim person. P is the British abbreviation for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense: the word once meant unlearned or uncultivated, as in 'rude mechanicals'.

clue.text: Queen is pressing clergyman about missile carriers (7)

indicators.note: IS squeezes around the next piece
turned about, so backwards

explanation.surface: The Queen is leaning on a vicar about rockets.
explanation.walkthrough: Missiles here are arrows, not rockets, and QU is a standard abbreviation for queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: an archer's case holds arrows, the oldest missiles.

clue.text: Upright piano kept inside also got damaged (8)

indicators.note: P is held within the other letters
the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An upright piano stored indoors was damaged as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright piano' is a real instrument; the clue splits it, so 'Upright' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the two vertical posts of a goal are its uprights.

clue.text: Mr. Bean crashed into middle of cement barrier (8)

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked and its parts scattered, so the letters are rearranged
'into' as in going inside something, so the jumbled letters go within ME
'middle' as the centre of the word, so only its central letters

blocks.note: the central two letters of cement

explanation.surface: Mr Bean smashes his car into a concrete wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble splits the central pair, sitting between their two letters. Mr Bean is the bumbling comic character played by Rowan Atkinson.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin sheet of tissue or material that separates two regions acts as a barrier.

clue.text: Brow of elevated promontory topped by bare tree (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means read upwards
in a down clue, the second piece sits above
stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: tree with its outer letters removed
a head is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: The brow of a raised headland is crowned by a leafless tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brow of elevated promontory' reads as one hilltop phrase; 'of' is part of the wordplay, turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the part of the face above the eyebrows is the brow.

clue.text: Stirring up protest, they throw objects! (7)

indicators.note: stirring something up churns it about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Agitators whip up a protest and hurl things.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the pun: 'throw' is the craft word for shaping clay on a wheel, not hurling missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: craftspeople who throw pots on a wheel make ceramic objects.

clue.text: Gambling Mecca in Grenoble (4)

indicators.note: the answer lies within the next word

blocks.note: the second to fifth letters of the French city

explanation.surface: A casino destination in the French city of Grenoble.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mecca is any place that draws crowds of a particular kind; here, a Nevada casino city.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Nevada city calls itself the Biggest Little City and is known for casinos.

clue.text: Necromancer is reportedly captivated by protégé (6)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so use the sound of the word
'captivated' in its literal sense of taken captive, so held inside the next word

blocks.note: a ward is someone under another's protection

explanation.surface: A sorcerer is said to be spellbound by his young apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captivated' reads as enchanted, fitting the sorcerer; its job is the literal sense, held captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a necromancer summons the dead by magic, and a wizard is any practitioner of magic.

clue.text: Angel fish circling bottom of wide river (6)

indicators.note: going round the other letters
in a down clue, the last letter

blocks.note: a chub is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angelfish swimming round the far end of a broad river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel fish' is one creature in the surface; split it: 'Angel' is the definition and 'fish' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this winged child-like figure belongs to one of the orders of angels.

clue.text: Proverbs 11 divides mother and son (6)

indicators.note: splits the other word by going into it
'and' in its plain sense of plus, so S is added at the end

explanation.surface: A Bible verse, Proverbs 11, drives a wedge between mother and son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proverbs 11' reads as a chapter of the Bible; the number splits off as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: short sayings of general truth.

clue.text: Inquisitive navigators originally discovered cetaceans respire (6)

indicators.note: 'originally' means at the origin, so the letter each word starts with
with its covering removed, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: whales = cetaceans, minus the W and S

explanation.surface: Curious sailors first spotted whales breathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' seems to belong with the navigators finding whales; it means uncovered, the outer letters taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: respiring is breathing, and drawing air in is half of it.

clue.text: Mix up stuff bishop left in storage on vacation (8)

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside
emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A bishop's belongings got muddled in storage while he was on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' looks like a holiday; it means empty the word, leaving the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to jumble things into disorder, as with eggs or a signal.

clue.text: Having acquired knowledge about home working (2,2)

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone who has learned about working from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a remote-working expert; the phrase is the one used of sharing a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be party to a secret or plan is to know about it.

clue.text: Successor pronounced most of island free of earth? (8)

indicators.note: said out, so a sound-alike

blocks.note: Borneo, the island, without its last letter

explanation.surface: The heir apparent announced that most of the island had been freed from the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: off the ground rather than clean of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: flying means being off the ground, so free of the earth.

clue.text: Illegally record detective meeting informant beside base (6)

indicators.note: 'meeting' as in coming together, so the two pieces join
'beside' in its sense of next to, so E is set alongside

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A detective meets his informant by a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' in the surface is a military one; in the wordplay it is the mathematical constant.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific sense of the verb: copying films or music without permission, as sea robbers took goods.

clue.text: Day worker on westbound underground is first-timer (8)

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left
'on' as in added on, so ANT is attached after the rest

blocks.note: the Tube is the London Underground

explanation.surface: A day labourer riding the westbound Tube for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground railway, so the surface is a commuter's first journey.
explanation.definitionFit: From French début, a first appearance; the word names someone making one.

clue.text: A post about Celsius scale (6)

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around, so the verb for posting wraps round C

blocks.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: A temperature scale in degrees Celsius is posted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celsius scale' reads as a temperature scale, but 'scale' is the verb, meaning to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to climb up a wall or mountain.
